title: Etale local Kummer monoid chart criterion
statement:
Let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Use the characteristic definition of Kummer in [def-per-kummer-log-morphism] and the chart definition of log etale in [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Then $f$ is Kummer etale if and only if it admits the following local chart data. There is a family of commutative squares $f_i:U_i\to V_i$ over $f:X\to Y$ with $U_i\to X$ and $V_i\to Y$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], the $U_i$ jointly covering $X$, and the log structures on $U_i,V_i$ pulled back from $X,Y$. The schemes $U_i,V_i$ may be chosen affine. There are fs monoids $P_i,Q_i$ with charts on $V_i,U_i$ and compatible homomorphisms $h_i:P_i\to Q_i$ such that $h_i$ and $h_i^{\rm gp}$ are injective, every $q\in Q_i$ has a positive multiple in $h_i(P_i)$, and $C_i=Q_i^{\rm gp}/h_i^{\rm gp}(P_i^{\rm gp})$ is finite and annihilated by an integer $n_i\geq1$ invertible on $V_i$. The comparison map
$$c_i:U_i\longrightarrow V_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P_i]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q_i]$$
is etale. The monoid rings and comparison maps are those of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], and the displayed product is the ordinary scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Neither finiteness nor surjectivity of $f$, nor log regularity, sharpness of the chart monoids, or flatness of the underlying $f$ is required.

source.place: Expose VI 2.1--2.2, printed pp.71--72: definition of Kummer etale, standard Kummer covers, and the assertion that every Kummer etale morphism is etale locally standard. The etale-comparison form is the local chart criterion (cf. X Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--138). No Stacks tag states this logarithmic assertion.

proof.text: First record precisely what strict etale localization preserves. For an etale map and a chosen geometric point, [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies its strict local ring with that downstairs. The germ formula of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the inverse-image log stalk with the original stalk, compatibly with multiplication. In the associated-log pushout defining the pulled-back log structure, the unit groups are therefore already identified; hence the log stalk and its characteristic are unchanged. Thus characteristic Kummer maps can be checked after these localizations. Every geometric point lifts through a jointly surjective etale family by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. A target neighbourhood can be accompanied by its ordinary base change on the source, etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Affine shrinking and composition retain etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. All these neighbourhoods remain locally Noetherian: etale implies locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies. These facts will be used in both directions.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69 (etale log structures); VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72 (etale localization); expansion using the cited stalk and scheme tools.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is Kummer etale in [def-per-kummer-log-morphism]. In particular it is log etale in [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. It is log smooth by [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. By [lem-per-fs-log-infinitesimal-criterion] its underlying map is locally of finite presentation and every strict square-zero test square of fine log schemes has exactly one global log lift. These imply the hypotheses of [lem-per-infinitesimal-log-differential-calculus]: unique global lifting implies etale-local existence, and the criterion also applies after compatible etale localization (restrict the chart data using step 1). Its last sentence therefore gives $\omega_f=0$. Here $\omega_f$ denotes relative logarithmic differentials; its geometric stalk therefore has the empty basis. This uses the unique-lifting clause, not just formal smoothness.

source.place: XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252: specialize the differential-basis construction to log etale maps; VI 2.1, p.71. The vanishing is supplied by the cited infinitesimal lemmas.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ with image $\bar y$. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] on $Y$ with the trivial group: all its hypotheses hold since its order is $1$. This gives a chart $P\to M_Y$ near $\bar y$, with $P=\overline M_{Y,\bar y}$ sharp fs. Use step 1 to make its neighbourhood $V$ affine and replace the source by the compatible strict etale neighbourhood above it. The base-changed source map is a strict base change of $f$, hence still log smooth by [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]; this is needed because the next lemmas fix a chart on the whole target. The same lemma on $X$ identifies $R=\overline M_{X,\bar x}$ as sharp fs. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], applied to the unit face of these sharp monoids, $P^{\rm gp}$ and $R^{\rm gp}$ are finite free. Set $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=M_{X,\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ and $D=A^\times\subset B$, so $B/D=R^{\rm gp}$. Apply [lem-per-log-smooth-differential-generators] to this fixed $P$-chart. Its basis has length $r=0$ by step 2. It supplies $n\geq1$ invertible in $A$, $n$-divisibility of $D$, and a finite cokernel killed by $n$ for $P^{\rm gp}\to B/D$. The strict local ring map from $\bar y$ to $\bar x$ is local, so an integer invertible at $\bar x$ is invertible at $\bar y$. Shrink $V$ to the open where $n$ is a unit and then affine-shrink again; restrict the source above it. The $P$-chart is unchanged, and now $n$ is invertible everywhere on $V$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), p.75, with trivial stabilizer; XVI 3.6.3 proof and footnote, p.252 (sharp base chart, differential generators and divisible units).

proof.text: Let $L=P^{\rm gp}$ and let $\varphi:L\to B$ be pullback of the fixed chart germ. Apply [lem-per-divisible-unit-lattice-extension] to $(L,B,D,\varphi,n)$; the finite-free, torsion-free quotient, finite-cokernel and divisible-unit hypotheses were all verified in step 3. Obtain $i:L\hookrightarrow G$ and $h:G\to B$ with $hi=\varphi$, where $G$ is finite free, $G/i(L)$ is killed by $n^k$ for some $k\geq0$, and $\rho:G\to B/D=R^{\rm gp}$ is surjective. In fact $\rho$ is injective. For $g\in\ker\rho$, write $n^kg=i(p)$ with $p\in P^{\rm gp}$. Then $\overline f^{\rm gp}(p)=0$. The Kummer hypothesis says $\overline f:P\to R$ is injective; its group map is injective too, since equality of differences reduces to equality in the integral monoids. Hence $p=0$. The free group $G$ is torsion-free, so $g=0$. Thus $\rho$ is an isomorphism. This is the point where characteristic Kummer injectivity removes possible extra chart units.

source.place: XVI 3.6.3--3.6.4, pp.252--253: lattice extension. The kernel calculation is the explicit Kummer specialization of that construction.

proof.text: Define $Q=h^{-1}(M_{X,\bar x})\subset G$, the prescribed inverse-image monoid to be used in step 6. A group element of $B$ lies in $M_{X,\bar x}$ exactly when its image in $R^{\rm gp}$ lies in $R$: choose a monoid element of that characteristic and multiply by the residual unit. Therefore $Q=\rho^{-1}(R)$. The map $P\to Q$ is $p\mapsto i(p)$, since $hi(p)=f^\flat(p)$. It is injective. Given $q\in Q$, characteristic Kummerness supplies $a>0$ and $p\in P$ with $a\rho(q)=\overline f(p)=\rho i(p)$; injectivity of $\rho$ gives $aq=i(p)$. Thus this monoid map is Kummer. Once $Q^{\rm gp}=G$ is identified in the next step, its group cokernel is $G/i(P^{\rm gp})$. It is finite: for a finite set of generators of $G$, coefficients modulo $n^k$ represent every quotient element. It is killed by $n^k$, an integer invertible on $V$. If $n=1$ or $k=0$ the quotient is trivial.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252, inverse-image monoid. Elementary kernel and positive-multiple calculation following step 4.

proof.text: Now apply [lem-per-kato-lattice-chart-realization] with its base monoid denoted here by $P$, $r=0$, the empty differential basis from step 2, and the $n,G,i,h$ of steps 3--4. The base group is torsion-free, $f$ is log smooth, $n$ is a unit at $\bar x$, $hi=\varphi$, the lattice quotient is killed by a power of $n$, and $\rho$ is surjective, exactly as that statement requires. It concludes that this very $Q=h^{-1}(M_{X,\bar x})$ is fs, that $Q^{\rm gp}=G$, and that on a pointed etale neighbourhood $U$ it gives a compatible chart and an etale comparison $U\to V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$. Thus step 5 gives every required monoid and finite-cokernel condition for these charts. Affine-shrink $U$ using step 1; the comparison remains etale by composition. Perform this construction at every point of $X$. The resulting $U$ jointly cover $X$, and the maps $U\to X$ and $V\to Y$ are etale composites of the chosen neighbourhood maps. This proves the forward implication without asserting that $f$ itself is finite or surjective.

source.place: XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252: prescribed inverse-image chart and etale comparison; VI 2.2, p.72: the local standard Kummer form.

proof.text: Conversely, assume the stated chart data. The kernel of each $h_i^{\rm gp}$ is zero. The finite cokernel $C_i$ has invertible order on $U_i$: by [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure], each nontrivial prime-power cyclic factor of a finite group killed by $n_i$ has prime dividing $n_i$. Since $n_i$ is a unit on $V_i$, all such primes, hence the product of the factor orders, are units on $U_i$. The trivial kernel has order $1$. Together with the etale comparison and the covering chart family, these are precisely the log-etale conditions of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. It remains to verify characteristic Kummerness; it is not inferred merely from the injectivity of the unsharpened chart map.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72 (standard Kummer covers are log etale); chart definition recalled in X 1.2, pp.136--138.

proof.text: Work in one chart at a geometric point $u$ of $U_i$ with image $v$ in $V_i$, and abbreviate $P_i,Q_i,h_i$ by $P,Q,h$. Let $F\subset P$ and $E\subset Q$ be the elements whose structural images are units at $v$ and $u$. They are faces because a product in a local ring is a unit exactly when both factors are units. The local ring map and chart compatibility give $h^{-1}(E)=F$. By [lem-trf-chart-face-localization-logification] the characteristics are $P_F/F^{\rm gp}$ and $Q_E/E^{\rm gp}$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] these embed in the group quotients $P^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ and $Q^{\rm gp}/E^{\rm gp}$, and the first quotient is torsion-free. For every $e\in E$, monoid Kummerness supplies $a>0$ and $p\in P$ with $ae=h(p)$. Its image is a unit at $u$, so $p\in F$ by reflection of units. Consequently each element of $E^{\rm gp}$ has a positive multiple in $h^{\rm gp}(F^{\rm gp})$ (write it as a difference of two elements of $E$ and take a common multiple).

source.place: VI 1.1 and 2.1--2.2, pp.69 and 71--72; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98: characteristic sharpening and face localization.

proof.text: If $p\in P^{\rm gp}$ maps to zero in $Q^{\rm gp}/E^{\rm gp}$, step 8 gives $a>0$ and $b\in F^{\rm gp}$ with $h^{\rm gp}(ap)=h^{\rm gp}(b)$. Its injectivity implies $ap=b$. The torsion-free group $P^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ then gives $p\in F^{\rm gp}$. Thus the induced characteristic group map, hence the characteristic monoid map, is injective. Every element of the source-side characteristic $Q_E/E^{\rm gp}$ has a representative $q\in Q$ (the denominator belongs to $E$ and disappears). Choose $a>0,p\in P$ with $aq=h(p)$; this proves the positive-multiple condition on characteristics. Therefore each localized log morphism is Kummer. Step 1 lifts every geometric point of $X$ to some $U_i$ and identifies the pulled-back characteristic map with the original one, so $f$ is Kummer everywhere. Together with step 7, [def-per-kummer-log-morphism] says exactly that $f$ is Kummer etale. The empty-source case uses the empty family; trivial characteristic monoids and trivial cokernels are included in all the preceding calculations.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72: characteristic Kummer condition; elementary localization calculation completing step 8.

proof_origin.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72 and XVI 3.6.3--3.6.4, pp.252--253; explicit assembly of existing infinitesimal, lattice and face-localization lemmas.
